roots.meaning: ≈ to flow. Operator Fluxus (the flowing); operand Flumen (the stream). e.g. fluid, flux, influence, affluent. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to stand, to hold position. Operator Status (the standing); operand Statio (the station). e.g. status, station, stable, constant. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to carry, to bear. Operator Latio (the carrying); operand Latum (the carried). e.g. transfer, refer, relate, translate. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to lead, to draw forward. Operator Ductio (the leading); operand Ductus (the led path). e.g. conduct, produce, induce, duct. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to fall, to drop. Operator Casus (the falling); operand Casum (the fallen). e.g. cadence, decay, case, accident. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to rise, to spring upward. Operator Surrectio (the rising); operand Surrectum (the risen). e.g. surge, resurgence, insurgent, source. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to stretch, to extend toward a target. Operator Tensio (the stretching); operand Tentum (the target reached for). e.g. tend, extend, intend, tension. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to send, to release deliberately. Operator Missio (the sending); operand Missum (the sent thing). e.g. mission, transmit, emit, missile. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to turn, to change direction. Operator Versio (the turning); operand Vertex (the turned point). e.g. convert, reverse, vertex, version. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to break, to rupture by force. Operator Fractio (the breaking); operand Fractura (the broken thing). e.g. fracture, fragment, fragile, infringe. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to join, to yoke together. Operator Junctio (the joining); operand Junctura (the joint). e.g. junction, conjunction, juncture, join. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to loosen, to release from binding. Operator Solutio (the loosening); operand Solutum (the dissolved). e.g. solve, solution, dissolve, absolve. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to split, to cut apart with severance. Operator Scissio (the splitting); operand Scissum (the split thing). e.g. rescind, scission, abscissa. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to grow, to increase from within. Operator Crescentia (the growing); operand Crementum (the increment). e.g. crescent, increase, increment, decrease. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to place, to set down deliberately. Operator Positio (the placing); operand Positum (the placed thing). e.g. position, component, deposit, postpone. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to rise, to originate, to be born from nothing. Operator Origo (the originating); operand Ortus (the emerged thing). e.g. origin, original, orient, abort. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ bottom, base, that which nothing is beneath. Operator Fundatio (the grounding); operand Fundamentum (the foundation). e.g. fund, foundation, fundamental, profound. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ root, the hidden source of visible growth. Operator Radicatio (the rooting); operand Radicem (the root itself). e.g. radical, eradicate, radish. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ enclosed space, total boundary, the bolt. Operator Clausura (the sealing); operand Clausum (the sealed interior). e.g. cloister, claustrophobia, closure, clause. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ boundary, end, the limit beyond which nothing continues. Operator Finitio (the limiting); operand Finem (the limit point). e.g. finite, final, define, infinite. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.

≈ threshold, the exact point of crossing. Operator Liminatio (the threshold-holding); operand Limen (the threshold itself). e.g. liminal, subliminal, eliminate, preliminary. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ to change, to transform substance or nature. Operator Mutatio (the changing); operand Mutatum (the changed thing). e.g. mutate, mutual, commute, transmute. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.

≈ tension, sustained opposition without resolution. Operator Tensio (the tension-holding); operand Tentum (the thing held in tension). e.g. tension, tense, intense, extension. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ void, structured emptiness that enables. Operator Vacuatio (the emptying); operand Vacuum (the void itself). e.g. vacuum, vacant, evacuate, vacation. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.
≈ convergence, the point where multiple things meet. Operator Nexio (the converging); operand Nexum (the convergence point). e.g. nexus, connect, annex. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.

≈ to endure, to receive, to undergo without initiating. Operator Passio (the receiving); operand Passum (the received thing). e.g. patient, passion, passive, compatible. From the 26 Latin Jurisdictions.

syntax.meaning: ≈ the whole file. On the canvas: the outer frame.
≈ a function: def name(args): …. On the canvas: its own §Canvas.
≈ an async function. On the canvas: its own §Canvas.
≈ a class: a template for objects. On the canvas: a node with its methods.
≈ gives back a value and ends the function. On the canvas: node: gives.
≈ stores a value in a name: x = …. On the canvas: node.
≈ updates a value in place: x += …. On the canvas: node.
≈ assignment with a type hint. On the canvas: node.
≈ repeats for each item: for x in …. On the canvas: gate: =T each.
≈ repeats while a condition holds. On the canvas: gate: =T / =F.
≈ chooses a branch: if … else. On the canvas: gate: =T / =F.
≈ runs a block inside a context: with open(…). On the canvas: node.
≈ signals an error. On the canvas: node: raise.
≈ attempts a block and catches errors. On the canvas: node, with except gates.
≈ what to do when an error is caught. On the canvas: gate: error.
≈ checks a condition must be true. On the canvas: gate.
≈ brings in other modules. On the canvas: node.
≈ reaches a name outside the function. On the canvas: node.
≈ a statement that is just an expression, like a call. On the canvas: node.
≈ do nothing, leave a loop, skip to the next round. On the canvas: node.
≈ and / or. On the canvas: inside a condition.
≈ arithmetic: + − × ÷ …. On the canvas: inside an expression.
≈ not, −x. On the canvas: inside an expression.
≈ ==, <, in, is …. On the canvas: inside a condition.
≈ a one-line unnamed function. On the canvas: inside an expression.
≈ a one-line if: a if c else b. On the canvas: inside an expression.
≈ runs a function: f(x). On the canvas: listed as calls:.
≈ a member of something: obj.name. On the canvas: inside an expression.
≈ an item or slice: a[i]. On the canvas: inside an expression.
≈ a variable. On the canvas: inside an expression.
≈ a literal value: 3, 'text', True. On the canvas: inside an expression.
≈ collections. On the canvas: inside an expression.
≈ build a collection in one line. On the canvas: inside an expression.
≈ pause for a result, or produce values one at a time. On the canvas: node.
≈ what a function needs. On the canvas: the first node's needs:.
